items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1957-08-04
items.q: I want to ask about this band, the one picture you have with Roy Palmer and Lawrence Dewey and Sugar Johnny.

ctx.x: Oakland right where Crozac is. Dates have their back entrance that Hall is given back there. Old man Umpra used to play with dear with Tick Chambers. You heard to talk about Tick Chambers? Yes, the Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Well, Tickshaber was playing cornet, and this fellow, Lawrence Dewitt, was playing clarinet at that time with him. And the old man, Umpra, was playing cyborg, clarinet over there with him also. Well, after he left, well, and the…

You know, the rest of it. You know, it's just like, yeah, you see that voice note? Just like I said, well, I'm going to play in E-flat. All right, that voice note. Well, all the rest of the modern keys will follow right behind the system, brother. See? And every time they change, you can hear change, and in you lose. Is that going on here? Yes. Yes. I want to ask about this band, the one picture you have with Roy Palmer and Lawrence Dewey and Sugar Johnny. Yes, well, I'll tell you.

items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1961-01-19
items.q: when I first got him, he was playing with Amos Raleigh

ctx.x: Chicago girl now. See? See that? Is there anything about Roy Palmer that you can tell us?

Well, Roy Palmer, he was playing with, when I first got him, he was playing with Amos Raleigh. You know who I talk about Amos Raleigh? Yes. A corn-ed player. Well, he used to be with that, I believe if I'm mistaken, it was the Tulane Band. The Tulane Band. That was Amos Raleigh. He was a corn-ed player. Well, Amos, this fellow used to play with him. And, uh, this other fellow, what's the name again? He used to play tram on wood, him. And then he started going, he went to wood too. Well, I found it out and I don't…
No, he's still living. I saw him last year.
